title: Markdown Foundations
lead: Write, preview and connect documents in mAIcro.

sections.heading: Course objective
sections.html: Learn Markdown by building readable pages and a small connected wiki.

sections.heading: What you’ll learn
sections.html:
• Format text, headings, lists and tables.
  • Link pages and include media from File Storage.
  • Use code, diagrams and the Markdown browser to build a useful wiki.

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.html: The media lessons use the mAIcroverse wiki sample files.

title: AI Tasks
lead: Manage AI tasks and their output types through GraphQL.

sections.heading: Course objective
sections.html: Explore how AI tasks and the types they depend on can be configured through scripts.

sections.heading: What you’ll learn
sections.html:
• Create, inspect and update an AI task.
  • Understand why typed output requires a registered GraphQL type.
  • Try a document extraction task and its supporting type.

sections.heading: Take care
sections.html: The exercises change project configuration and create, update and delete example tasks and types.

title: Book Club
lead: Build a connected book-club dataset with GraphQL, graphs and search.

sections.heading: Course objective
sections.html: Bring several mAIcro capabilities together in a practical social-data example.

sections.heading: What you’ll learn
sections.html:
• Create and query tables through generated GraphQL operations.
  • Explore graph relationships, semantic search and asynchronous analysis.
  • Try team-scoped notes and a dashboard payload.

sections.heading: Take care
sections.html: Setup drops project tables and graph data before recreating the example. Use a disposable learning instance.

title: Memory Essentials
lead: Practise remembering, recalling and forgetting structured data.

sections.heading: Course objective
sections.html: Follow a complete lifecycle for persistent memory blocks.

sections.heading: What you’ll learn
sections.html:
• Create and read memory blocks and individual paths.
  • Update and remove values.
  • Use assertions to verify the results of each stage.

sections.heading: Take care
sections.html: The setup resets project memory blocks, including existing blocks.

title: Data Import
lead: Turn customer, order and weather files into dashboard-ready data.

sections.heading: Course objective
sections.html: Explore an import pipeline from source files through queryable tables and charts.

sections.heading: What you’ll learn
sections.html:
• Import and merge customer and order data.
  • Add optional analytics datasets.
  • Explore the dashboard payload and Charts panel.

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.html: This example uses the mAIcroverse customer-order sample files.

title: Data File Fetch
lead: Read CSV and JSONL files directly as GraphQL results.

sections.heading: Course objective
sections.html: Learn to query complete datasets stored in File Storage.

sections.heading: What you’ll learn
sections.html:
• Fetch JSONL records as an array.
  • Read CSV rows using their header names.
  • Recognise errors when files are missing or malformed.

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.html: The customer-order sample files must be present in File Storage.

title: Clients and Documents
lead: Build a client dataset and connect a document to a client.

sections.heading: Course objective
sections.html: Explore a small client-data workflow that combines tables and typed document relationships.

sections.heading: What you’ll learn
sections.html:
• Create and seed a clients table and reload the schema.
  • Configure a document relationship.
  • Query client records alongside a linked document.

sections.heading: Take care
sections.html: Setup clears demo client data and resets the linked document state.

title: HR Graph
lead: Model employment history with a graph and reusable operations.

sections.heading: Course objective
sections.html: Build an employment-tracking example using Apache AGE and GraphQL-wrapped Cypher.

sections.heading: What you’ll learn
sections.html:
• Model employees, employers and employment relationships.
  • Track changes over time.
  • Explore business rules enforced by graph operations.

sections.heading: Take care
sections.html: Setup wipes project data and uploaded files. Use a disposable learning instance.

title: API Wrappers
lead: Bring external REST APIs into your GraphQL schema.

sections.heading: Course objective
sections.html: Register and test GraphQL operations backed by external APIs.

sections.heading: What you’ll learn
sections.html:
• Map inputs and responses between GraphQL and an API.
  • Try a public example without an API key.
  • Explore provider credentials and rate limits for optional examples.

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.html: Some examples require external provider API keys and internet access.

title: Scheduled Weather Collector
lead: Collect weather readings on a schedule.

sections.heading: Course objective
sections.html: Build and inspect a scheduled ingestion workflow using cron jobs.

sections.heading: What you’ll learn
sections.html:
• Register a weather API wrapper and create a readings table.
  • Schedule a recurring collection script.
  • Inspect job status, errors and stored readings.

sections.heading: Take care
sections.html: Setup replaces cron jobs and recreates the weather readings table, deleting existing readings. Use a disposable learning instance.

title: ASX Watcher
lead: Explore market data, Markdown reports and browser automation.

sections.heading: Course objective
sections.html: Build a progression from raw ticker data to reports and browser-based extraction.

sections.heading: What you’ll learn
sections.html:
• Fetch and inspect market data.
  • Shape results into Markdown reports.
  • Navigate and extract information using browser automation.

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.html: The exercises use external websites and require internet access.

title: Browser Automation
lead: Build repeatable browser workflows with Browser X4m.

sections.heading: Course objective
sections.html: Learn browser sessions, page interaction and extraction through practical exercises.

sections.heading: What you’ll learn
sections.html:
• Open, manage and close browser sessions.
  • Interact with forms, selectors and uploads.
  • Extract page data and capture screenshots in an end-to-end workflow.

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.html: Examples interact with external pages and require browser and network access.

title: AI Signatures and Types
lead: Define clear input and output contracts for AI signatures.

sections.heading: Course objective
sections.html: Create and evolve AI signatures supported by explicit GraphQL types.

sections.heading: What you’ll learn
sections.html:
• Register supporting types and create signatures.
  • Run and inspect signatures alongside their type definitions.
  • Check valid and invalid inputs and clean up example types.

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.html: Running the examples requires configured AI services.

sections.heading: Take care
sections.html: The exercises create and delete example signatures and types.

title: Forms
lead: Explore a multi-step form and its submission workflow.

sections.heading: Course objective
sections.html: Build and inspect an aged-care intake form with realistic demonstration submissions.

sections.heading: What you’ll learn
sections.html:
• Create a structured multi-step form definition.
  • Explore saved responses and grouped submissions.
  • Use the Forms panel to switch between example submissions.

sections.heading: Take care
sections.html: Setup rebuilds the demo form and replaces its previous demo submissions.
